utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Professor Aleksandric, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Ms. Issa, the Chamber encourages you to really focus on what will be the matters in dispute and not to go through everything that is already clearly there on paper. In view of the meanwhile-disclosed French report, for example, I can imagine that that creates some issues which might cause some dispute at a later stage. Some of the issues are known already, so therefore instead of leading us through a lot of material which is, if not the same, almost the same of what we've seen already and not very likely to create great dispute, you're encouraged to focus on the matters I just mentioned. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've actually attempted to rework my examination-in-chief with that in mind. Your Honour, perhaps before we begin I'd just like the witness to be handed up a copy of his 92 ter statement which we have and given to Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: As well as his attached reports which are annexes to that statement to assist him in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, just very briefly, Professor Aleksandric. We stopped yesterday when you were explaining that -- that you found some electric cables at the Ekonomija farm. Have you ever been to a farm or heard of a situation in which electric cables were used to tie-up animals?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I understand that my client is not receiving transmission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it should be fixed. I take it that he is on the right channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Okay. We're back again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Professor Aleksandric, could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to whether I was there before the 11th of September, 1998, no, I was never there before at the Ekonomija farm. As far as the electrical cables are concerned, I recalled something as I returned to the hotel room. I said yesterday that a piece of the cable was found by the body marked as R-8. However, I also recall that there was a piece of cable found by the body marked as R-13. It is general knowledge that cattle is not tied up in the shed with the use of electrical cable because it can harm them. As far as the pieces of burnt paper are concerned, they were found at the level at which the cables were found, and only the following inference can be drawn from there. I was able to examine between 150 to 200 persons who were lucky enough to survive the camps in Bosnia. I heard all manner of stories about how they had been tortured --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll stop you there --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Therefore, this image --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was waiting to see where this would lead. We do want to keep this to a minimum. But we've now gone through the observations of the witness and if we're moving on to the stage where conclusions are to be drawn in my submission those are outside --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness started telling us there was only one inference possible and he didn't draw an inference but he started telling us what he experienced in Bosnia which he is permitted to do. But the inferences there seem not to be within his field of expertise. Nevertheless, his experience in this respect might be relevant, so therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Certainly, but not the conclusions is my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- what he's seen in the circumstances of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he can tell us what we has seen in other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, the observations there's no objection to but not the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The answer at this point is non-responsive to the question asked; in addition, the question was dealing specifically with issues concerning cables and the witness at this point is a bit far afield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I take it yesterday the question was already about papers as well. So therefore that would be the next observation. Let's try to proceed as efficiently as possible. Professor Aleksandric, you may have noted that the Defence has some difficulties in where you go -- where you would go beyond your own expertise, I would say that the -- your experience as we have -- read from your statement, your experience on what you see would be the physical effect of -- of the situation you found there, certainly within your field of expertise. Any further inferences to be drawn as to what caused people perhaps to create a situation as you found it might not be within your field of expertise. If you would please keep that in mind, then please continue to tell us about what you were telling us, that is, your experience in Bosnia. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, if you can perhaps continue JUST to finish up your answer, Professor Aleksandric.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I had occasion to examine between 150 to 200 persons who survived torture in camps. On the basis of this experience and on the basis of the facts found at the Ekonomija farm, I wanted to present you with my expert opinion, if you'll allow me to; if you deny me that possibility, then there's nothing I can do about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I do not deny you at all. Please tell us what it is. And if anyone thinks that any opinion you express would not be within your field of expertise, then we'll hear. But we do not know yet what opinion you are going to express. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the facts established at the Ekonomija farm concerning the cables and pieces of paper and on the basis of the fact that the same piece of cable was found by the body R-13 and on the basis of my personal experience, it is my expert opinion that the burnt paper and the fact that the people were tied up by cables, it is my opinion that they had to put out the fire burning by their own feet --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's, I think, not something your expertise would tell you, whether this happened. What your expertise might perhaps tell us is that you found similar situations in which people had on the basis of what then appeared later -- I mean, burning pieces of paper and wire, I fully do understand that on the basis of your experience brought into your mind similar situations in which, as I understand, it was established that people had to put out the fire with their feet. Is that how I should understand your testimony? Whether that happened here of course is another matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just moving on then, Professor Aleksandric, you described the methodology of recovering the bodies at the Lake Radonjic in quite some detail in your statement and I'm not going to ask you to repeat that. But you do mention in paragraph 36 of your statement that you -- you and your team placed a number on -- and without the letter "R" on the outside of a body-bag once a body was contained in the bag and -- and you also placed a number on the inside -- the same number on the inside of the body-bag and you say that there was no letter R placed on the outside of the bag because the police labels were easier to use and the police did not use letters and we used pieces of paper to label the inside of the bags. So my question is: Why is it that labels were used both inside and outside the body-bags?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As can be seen on the videos, initially when we marked all the bodies that were visible from numbers 1 to 10, we used numerical markings. And one -- a cardboard cone was marked with the number -- the letter, rather, "R", which applied to that location. We opted for the dual marking of the body-bags by putting the letter "R" and next to it the number on the cardboard that was outside. This piece of cardboard was then stuck to the body-bag. We were afraid that it would easily fall off. That's why we placed the piece of cardboard inside since the police markings did not have the possibility of marking them with the number -- with the letter, rather. That's why inside we placed the marking -- the full marking with the letter and the number, and the other label was placed outside. This facilitated the transportation of the body-bags to Hotel Pastrik, the fact that we had a label on the outside of it rather than to have to open each one of the body-bags in order to know which bodies were contained inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of placing the label inside the body-bag?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not place any labels inside. We placed a piece of cardboard which contained the letter and the relative number. We didn't put any stickers, and this was of course to facilitate the identification of the corpse that was inside a body-bag.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, that is so obvious. I mean, whether any mistakes were made is another matter. Why do you put a marker in a body-bag? To know at a later stage which body we are dealing with. That is so obvious and so self-evident, apart from whether any mistakes were made or there could be a confusion. That is really a question, to say it frankly, underestimates the mental abilities of this Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It wasn't done for that reason, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't take me too seriously on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning then to the bodies that you found in the Lake Radonjic canal area, when you compiled the statement, when you signed your statement, Professor Aleksandric, did you mark down the location of the bodies found on the Lake Radonjic canal area?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean whether I marked the location of the bodies on the map?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning to Exhibit P459, page 2, if you can look at your screen and we can then enlarge -- just zoom in on the centre part to see the markings, please. Is that -- are those your markings of the location of the bodies, Professor Aleksandric?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apologies, I don't have the image on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, if you want to have it on the screen, you can check under the e-court button whether it is -- or is it --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's on the video, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not sure if we're experiencing perhaps a technical problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Usually exhibits are shown on the -- under the e-court button, and Madam Registrar, since you have ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We're actually showing the exhibits through Sanction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do it by your own system, you know that Madam Registrar is able to show --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, it's okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the photograph on which I marked in my own hand the approximate location of the bodies found and marked with a specific number.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how did you get the distances as to the location of the bodies? You say the approximate location. Can you explain what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the approximate location because I did not have the exact location in centimetres. In my country the scene of crime investigation and the diagram itself is done by the investigating judge and the scene of crime officers. I produced these markings on the basis of what I had seen on the site and on the basis of my recollections. And I believe that it is not perhaps quite identical, but it is very much close to what was found on the site, on the video, and on the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Turning then to P459, page 1, and we'll just zoom in on the top part. Would you indicate, are those your markings, Professor Aleksandric?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you've marked the bodies that were found in the natural part of the canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately. Again, this is the lower part of the canal and you can already see the point where the water from the canal flows into the lake.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Turning then to P615 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Could I before that's taken off the screen just to confirm for the record there is a date on the bottom of these photographs but when exactly these markings were made so that -- that that is clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could clarify that, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate, Professor Aleksandric, when you made these markings?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever can read can see that it says the 14th of June, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you actually made these markings at the same time that you -- you met with myself and others when you made your consolidated -- or 92 ter statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On page 1 of the report you gave to me, there is the exact date of my stay in The Hague, and that's the last day of my stay in The Hague, the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning then to P615. Now, we see an electronic version of that which is also on the larger map that's set up in the courtroom. Does that depict the markings that you've made, Professor Aleksandric, in electronic format? You can -- perhaps we can zoom-in.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Then focusing on the first body which you've labelled as R-1, you say in your statement at paragraph 63 that the body marked as R-1 was found on the ground with a plastic sack pulled over the upper half and a jute sack pulled over the lower half. Turning to Exhibit P600 at photograph 102, can you just very briefly indicate what that photograph depicts, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the cone is with the number 1 is the place where the body was in the sack. When we turned over the sack, new bones appeared underneath and then you can see the lower leg bone. And then we saw that underneath the body marked as 1 there is another body. When we dug further we didn't find just one body but two more bodies which we marked with the numbers 11 and 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You just mentioned two more bodies marked 11 and 12. Let me just ask you this first: Were you able to see those bodies before you removed body 1?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because the sack was over the bones. It was just like I said. The sack was moved from the place and then these other bones started to appear.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Then just focusing on bodies R-11, which was ultimately identified as the mother of Witness 4 and R-12 as we see depicted on the screen. You describe in paragraph 72 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just for the -- for your Chamber -- for the Chamber's reference, Your Honour, these photographs are also depicted in the photo album that was passed on to the Chamber yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You describe, sir, in paragraph 72 of your statement as two bodies that were found with their heads next to each other, one left and right shoe were found beside these bodies, as well as a rusty piece of barbed wire measuring 2.5 metres that was tied in a sliding noose at one end. Turning then to Exhibit 588, can you please indicate briefly what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a later stage than the one shown in the previous photograph. You can see the left foot here below the number. This is the foot that was peeking out with the lower leg bone and it was pointing in the direction where the other body parts were. Then we palpated when we found the number 11 body, we palpated with that head another head and concluded that there must be another body there. We continued to dig and then that next body we marked with a number 12. There is the photograph here which in a way shows the relationship between the two bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to -- just so that we're absolutely clear, the foot that you refer to relates to body 11. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you also mentioned, Professor Aleksandric, finding a rusty piece of barbed wire near these two bodies. I'm just going to show you a short video-clip, Exhibit 452, please, which starts at 003024, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you just indicate -- there's no transcript. If you can just indicate what we're looking at here, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looked at it from the way we shook the body off from the soil because it was intermingled with the soil. We brought the body-bag close in order to manipulate the body as little as possible, because if you take hold of one part of the body the rest would fall away because it was intermingled with the soil. So we just tried to turn over the body into the body-bag as much as this was possible. After that when we transferred most of the body - and you might see that later - you will see how we are trying to shake loose the remaining bones from the soil, because all the bodies were in an advanced stage of decomposition. They were practically decomposed. This is me in the green T-shirt, and I'm looking through the soil to make sure -- to see if there are any other fragments of the body bones that are left in the mud. The point was, first of all, to collect all the human remains from the location and as much as possible to determine if all of the remains belonged to one person or possibly to two, as you saw from the previous footage.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, we've just paused it at 0032129, and just for the record shortly before that the witness has identified himself picking through the bones and placing them in the body-bag. Perhaps if we can just continue on until the end of that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you appear to be holding something in your hand at 003236, what is that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Pause it there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little bit earlier, if you noticed when I jerked away, I got pricked and then perhaps if you saw the translation I asked for a stronger pair of gloves. And then as we went on we found the barbed wire and then you can see the barbed wire. We took out the bodies already, so we came with the barbed up -- found the barbed wire with the remaining parts of the bodies. So we really couldn't determine with which body the barbed wire went. In any case, we found it closer to body number 12 and that is why we put it together later with the body in body-bag 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, the screen paused with the barbed wire is at 003243.5.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say, Professor Aleksandric, you couldn't determine to which body it belonged to, you're referring now to -- between body 11 and 12. Is that correct? Just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically in between.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just turning then to Exhibit P506 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Issa, one clarifying question. You're talking about barbed wire between the two bodies. Was the barbed wire just loose of the bodies or would, for example, the barbed wire be around a body part? Do you understand what I mean, just to give you -- it could be around an arm, it could be next to the arm. Did you find at any moment that the barbed wire would have been in a position to go around a body or a body part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you saw, the body was in the soil first. We took out most of the body, and then as you see with my bare hands just in gloves, I was searching for the remaining bones. And then at the end I felt the barbed wire. It's very difficult to determine whether the barbed wire was wrapped around a body part or not. We didn't see that. But as I said, it was found next to the body and you saw me taking out the remaining parts of the bones. And while I was searching for more, I got pricked on the barbed wire and that's how I found the barbed wire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you notice anywhere nearby a barbed-wire fence, I understand barbed wire often used to keep cattle or animals within a certain area. Did you notice anywhere nearby a barbed-wire fence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The barbed wire was close to the farm. There were fruit orchards around the farm, a large area of land covered with plums or other fruit trees, and those land sections were wired off in order to prevent the cattle from getting in there and from destroying the fruit trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the nearest spot where you saw any such barbed wire fence, could you tell us at what distance that would have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was practically next to the farm, next to the farm building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least a couple of hundred metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 300 metres from what I can recall. That's what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Professor Aleksandric, when you mentioned just a moment ago that -- that it's next to the farm, are you able just to have a look at the aerial map that is behind you and just indicate the location of the -- of the farm and perhaps the fence that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that's an enlargement of Exhibit P615, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You can actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] This is Ekonomija --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Professor Aleksandric, we have problems if you do not adjust the microphones when you are standing, the interpreters might have difficulties to hear you. So if you would please keep -- stay as close to the microphone as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're just pointing now -- or you just pointed a moment ago for the record to the upper left-hand corner of the enlargement of P615 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do apologise, I wasn't able to see where he did it also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please point at the farm again where you said you saw barbed wire fences with the pointer, could you please point at it on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to give a broader explanation. This is the access road. This is the location where we found the group of bodies, and this road leads to the farm, and this is the farm building. The orchards are all around here and behind here, and from what I can recall I think there is a sketch of all this in the evidence material, and I think that exhibit is probably marked with the fruit trees that are planted there. In any case, the Ekonomija farm building is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are now pointing to the fruit trees planted from the building of the economic farm in the direction of Lake Radonjic, close to the farm buildings. Is that where you saw the barbed wire or did you see it any closer to the place where the bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The barbed wire was in this area here, around these fruit trees. But here the fence was destroyed. It wasn't practically -- none of it was left. Perhaps it was standing there at one point, but when we got there, there was hardly any of it left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness now also pointed at the area upstream from the economic farm where we find a pattern of stripes more or less of plantation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You can have a seat again, Professor Aleksandric, please. Now, just turning to Exhibit 506 very briefly, the middle photograph, please. Can you indicate what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph shows a body in a sack with barbed wire.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you indicate --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I can see also table legs; that means that the bag was opened in the improvised autopsy room at the Pastrik Hotel when we were carrying out the autopsies. And you can see the tables here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we just look at the top photo of that exhibit, we can see that the label on that in relation to that body is 12?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is body 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So just to clarify, you said earlier, Professor Aleksandric, that you didn't know which -- which body to attribute the barbed wire to. Is there any particular reason you decided to attribute it to body 12?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He just told us that it was closest to that body.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: He only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are seeking any other explanation, fine, but if that's what --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- your question was about --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's fine. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In paragraph 257 of your statement, Professor Aleksandric, you say that bodies on the surface were likely present at the spot for a couple of weeks, but the bodies underneath the surface were probably there for a few more weeks than those found on the surface. This means that the bodies underneath the surface had likely been there for a few months. Firstly, can you indicate what is the basis of your conclusion that the surface bodies had been there for a few weeks?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the degree of decomposition, the advanced stage of the rotting of the bodies; secondly, the position of the bodies, they were either mixed in with the soil at the surface but they were not covered over completely by the soil. Compared to, for example, body number 14 and number 15, where we only found the bones underneath a pile of stone which was not naturally there. Because if the water had brought the pebbles in a natural way just to clean the bodies, I'm talking about bodies 14 and 15, there was a difference in the degree of decomposition changes. The bodies that were on the surface were mixed in with the soil and the other bodies were deeper in the soil. Being familiar with the process of decomposition and in view of the fact that it was summer with high temperatures and the area where rains are frequent, I believe that the bodies on the surface had been lying there for several weeks and those that were deeper and where the mortal remains were just bones had been there for several weeks longer than the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any other bodies that you found that were underneath a body similar to the situation that we just saw which is R-11 and -12 being found underneath R-1?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A new body was found underneath R-3 marked as R-13. And when we were digging at the end, just to probe the terrain to see if there was anything else there, then we found body 16 some 30 centimetres deeper, and then even deeper than that we found body number 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But just to clarify, bodies 16 and 17 were not underneath other bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So dealing then with R-13 and -3 --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I just explained that 17 was underneath 16, in that sense was what I said. Otherwise, they were not underneath other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And 16 was below the surface; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It was 30 centimetres below the surface.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to -- focusing then very briefly on R-3 and R-13, R-3 was identified as Misin Berisha and R-13 identified as Idriz Hoti. Can you first indicate, was R-13, Idriz Hoti, visible underneath R-3 before having removed R-3, Misin Berisha?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Even R-3 from what I can recall only had parts of his trousers showing, and of course parts of the leg bones in the trousers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just turning then to P594 very briefly, photograph number 33.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You can focus in on the label, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just very briefly, can you indicate what -- what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows our method of work or a part of it, and that is the marking of the body-bag at the end before it was closed up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And this is -- this is taking place at the scene in the canal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Professor, I want to talk to you about finding a noose, an electric cable, and a metal wire in the -- in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, before you continue, let me just try to be very clear to you. The other report has now been disclosed to the Chamber that is not in evidence but of course we read what is in there. And it turns out in relation to R-14 specific reasons are given why other experts have a different opinion on the time the body was there. Why not ask this witness whether he paid any attention to those circumstances which seems to be relevant for the other experts because that most likely will be a matter that will be in dispute rather than to have the witness just repeat -- well, clarify a tiny little bit what is already in his report. That was -- I just give you this one example of what most likely will be the core of the dispute between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please try to focus on where we could expect -- I mean, I expect the Defence to focus on the matters you consider solid. At the same time, it's not that I'm asking your attention to what the Defence might raise at a later stage. But also, of course, I would expect the same from the Defence. And I do not know, but I can imagine that this French report which was made on the request of -- of the Prosecution, sooner or later if this case continues might ever become evidence, if that's the intention then we could already perhaps anticipate on it. I mean, it has been disclosed also to the Chamber because it was late disclosure, not to be blamed, but it was late disclosure and therefore it has been -- so therefore I would very much like you to focus on these kind of things rather than to ask: Is this the marking of the bodies in the canyon? Because of course that is not the concrete part of the canal; that is the canyon. We have heard that approximately 70 or 80 times by now. We're perfectly able to see when markings are about the lower stream, that that's the canyon and not the concrete part of the canal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder if I might finish up a couple of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I do take Your Honour's direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can refer to paragraph 98 of your statement, Professor Aleksandric. You say in paragraph 98 that a black cable was found, you just mentioned that yesterday and today as well, that this cable was the same type as the one found at the Ekonomija farm. And I just want to refer you to an exhibit, P604, number 154, please. Just briefly, can you indicate what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts a coil of alpinist or climbing rope and then in the middle you can see the stiff electrical cable which has the same characteristics as the cable found at the Ekonomija.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can then just go to body R-8, just if we can focus on that. Now, you mention in paragraph 111 of your statement that you found a body marked R-8, a majority of it was covered by earth so that only pieces of clothing and bones were visible. The body was carefully uncovered together with all its fragments that could be found. We found a tight noose made of mountain-climbing rope surrounding the neck area. This rope was approximately 1 centimetre thick and its circumference corresponds to the circumference of an average neck on a normal adult. Turning then to Exhibit 452, I just want to show you a very brief video-clip which begins at 005249.7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found one end of the rope here. That is my knee. Next to my left knee you can see skulls. This is a little bit further away. This is something else. This is in the canal itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see I am trying when we cleared away the soil from the skull and freed the rope, I tried to pull out the rope that was around the neck area, and here you can see already a part of the noose. So we were practically working in the same way as an archaeologist would work. And then when we pulled the noose out, perhaps that is also shown to -- that the noose is the size of the neck of an average adult. And this is the position in which we found the noose.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just for the record we are now -- the noose that you're referring to is at 005333.2. And I'm just going to ask that this be played and fast-forwarded slightly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if we can pause it there, please. Whose arm is that that we see depicted holding this noose as you described earlier at 005355.1?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my arm.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, would the case be any different if it would be someone else's arm, one of the assistants or one of the colleagues?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it wouldn't be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I was simply asking him to identify the clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Turning to bodies R-14 and R-15, just focusing on those bodies, in paragraph 134, Professor Aleksandric, you say that about 2 metres to the right of body R-10 from the direction of the canal at the end of the concrete wall of the canal from its outer side, there was a pile of gravel on which there were no pieces of human bones. However, since there was projectile damage on the wall above this wall, there was a possibility that a body was located underneath the gravel so we carefully removed the gravel. My question is: Why did the projectile damage on the wall cause you to search underneath the pile of gravel?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the damage was inflicted by projectiles; secondly, we had a large pile of gravel there. At the end of the day, this wasn't the first time I was performing that job. I have extensive professional experience. We had our suspicions that there were bodies beneath the pile of gravel, and indeed we found some.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And just turning then very briefly to Exhibit 452, that's another clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: At 010617.8, can you just indicate briefly what we're looking at there, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the projectile damage on the wall marked with arrows.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can play that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just if we could briefly stop there, please. 010637.5.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just indicate briefly what we're looking at there, Professor Aleksandric.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire footage shows that beneath the projectile damage on the wall and beneath the gravel which we removed, we found some footwear and parts of bone that cannot be seen that well. And another thing that one cannot see very well there is number "R".

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But we do see a label there marked 14. Is that correct, Professor Aleksandric?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You can just continue that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What if the witness would have said: No, we do not see a 14. Ms. Issa, we can read, we can look, we have eyes, we have even some brains. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate that, but I noted it for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's for the purposes of the transcript, ultimately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think you mentioned exactly what picture we are looking at. Okay, then if that's necessary, then I might have been too quickly, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. We can continue that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the other pile of bones marked with number 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again with shoes and parts of bone. You can see that the bones are entirely without any soft tissue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And that's at, for the record, 010651.3. We can then just move on turning to Exhibit P596.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Issa, a very practical way if there's such an obvious thing to see, then I don't think that the Defence would oppose if Ms. Issa herself would see we are now looking at -- we see 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that goes quicker. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just going back to what the image that we just saw, Professor. What was the significance of finding the bare bones under the concrete wall at the body labelled 15?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I know we're now heading into an area where once again the testimony could be outside of the expertise of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could be --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let's wait and see what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's on the record, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- Out of caution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Professor Aleksandric, are you able to answer that, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate, Professor Aleksandric, what was the significance of finding the bare bones that you just noted in that video that was attributed to body 15 underneath the concrete wall?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general significance that any recovered body carries. We found bodies 14 and 15 behind the pile of gravel, which could not have ended up naturally there. It could not have been washed-up there by the water. It was quite evident that the pile was man-made.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is there any significance to finding those bones on the pile of gravel as to your ability to assess the time of death for that particular body?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean specifically in relation to number 15? But let me tell you first, generally speaking, in relation to the damage inflicted by the projectiles. We can see on photograph 76 and 74 the mutual relationship of the bodies and their relationship with the projectile damage. You can see the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the position of the bodies 14 and 15 in relation to the projectile damage on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have gone into that area. In my submission this witness is not an expert in ballistics, in projectiles, in the direction that bullets take, where they might have been fired from, whether or not are any bodies were therefore in a line of a projectile. And the ultimate conclusion which we have objected to in his report at paragraphs 47 to 49 that this was some kind of execution site, those are all conclusions that he doesn't have expertise to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether he has drawn any conclusions. He made observations of the position of the bodies in relation to the bullet marks and that is -- as a witness he is -- certainly may have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: These are his observations but as to where the bullets may have been fired from is the next step.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I'm anticipating that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's wait what the next step will be and not always guess on what the next step will be, then object against the next step. If there comes an area where you say the witness could not have made this observation or could not have made, on the basis of his expertise, made this inference, then we'll -- I would first like to hear such an inference being made rather than to anticipate what will -- I mean, and then the objection might stand just as good as the anticipatory objections which certainly disrupted the flow of evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm basing it on the statement which, I think, is what Ms. Issa is going to be taking the witness through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see what happens. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Professor Aleksandric, you just mentioned that by looking at this array, if we can perhaps focus on picture 75, please. Now, we see what's depicted in that photograph, bodies labelled as 3, 4, 5, and 7, which are immediately below the concrete wall in which you've described there were bullet-holes. Focusing on body R-5 for the moment, who was ultimately identified as Xhevat Berisha, I would just like you to have a look at Exhibit P601 at 106. Can you indicate, Professor Aleksandric, what that photograph depicts there, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a body in trousers and a blue sweater, and it is positioned just as it was when we saw it first. And you can see in that piece of clothing bullet marks. It's bullet-riddled.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say that piece of clothing, you're referring to the blue sweater, for the record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Was there any significance about this -- these -- these bullet-holes in the blue sweater, given the location of the -- of the body when you found it? What was significant about that to you?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the bullet-holes; secondly, an autopsy of the body established that there were -- there was damage inflicted to the bones as a result of these bullets. All the nine bodies, therefore, from 1 to 10 that we found on the surface of the earth - and don't forget number 6 was marked with a slipper - only 9 didn't have damage to the bones. If you look at this body, number 5, their mutual relationship, their positioning in relation to the wall -- well, I'll leave it up to the Chamber to draw their conclusions, whether such persons with such injuries and such -- with the bullet-holes and the damage that can be seen, whether they were, indeed, executed there on the spot or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I refer you, Professor Aleksandric, you mentioned that -- that in the autopsy there was an indication that there was damage to the bones to all these bodies, and -- including body 5. I just want to draw your attention to Exhibit P672 [sic]. This was the autopsy report prepared by Professor Hoff-Olsen --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Which is not in dispute, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just to refer to the summary on the very first page of the report were you aware that Professor Hoff-Olsen determined that the cause of death was, in fact, gun-shot wound to the head and that the additional finding it would be possible that the victim died from a gun-shot wound to the trunk. Were you aware of that, Professor Aleksandric?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We can zoom in on the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this is the first time I see or hear this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, Madam Registrar has some difficulties in understanding P672 because she's aware, I think, up till 615, or at least not up to 672. So you're now using --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we've actually recently -- more recently added that exhibit and it's P617.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's 65 ter number 913, page 8, if that assists Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just -- I just want to indicate, Your Honour, that in view of the time I am about to proceed -- to move to another area but I'm in Your Honour's hands as to when you'd like to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The break is usually at 10.30. Let me just -- you showed now the autopsy report -- yes, now we know that Professor Aleksandric for the first time hears this. What's the -- I mean, I'm just asking myself what to do with this answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I was just going to ask a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then please put the next question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can clarify there are a number of autopsy reports done by international forensic experts at a later point and these are the subject of agreed facts, so there's no need to go through each one of these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't know what Ms. Issa would like to ask him about. It could be whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: To save time, Your Honour, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Ms. Issa, there seems to be no dispute as to the correctness of that report, but I do understand you might have other reasons why you put it to the witness. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is -- are those findings, Professor Aleksandric, consistent with your observations of the bodies that were found below the wall, particularly body number 5?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say in this way, ad hoc, whether they are consistent with our findings. I would have to examine thoroughly both sets of findings to be able to tell you that. However, I specifically note that on body number 5, we found projectile damage. But I can't tell you anything more than that. I would have to consult the documentation and compare. I told you that we found out of the nine bodies on the surface only on bodies number 7 and 9 we did not find any damage caused by projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving then to body number 9, specifically Exhibit 605, number 158. Can you indicate just briefly, Professor Aleksandric, what that photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the cone number 8 stands, you see the white piece of stone. And beneath it you can see parts of body and pieces of clothing protruding. That was body number 8. To the left, practically on the surface of the earth, is another body that we subsequently marked with number 9, or rather, not subsequently. It was already marked at that point in time but it must have been removed. And the photograph was only then taken. Why did we take the number away? Because it was more practical for us to remove body number 9 in order not to interfere with the digging out of the body number 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Turning then to Exhibit P469, this is the autopsy report from 1998, which I believe you've signed, as you indicate in your statement, you signed all the autopsy reports that relate to the recovery of the bodies in Lake Radonjic. If we can then just turn to page 2, paragraph 7, of that statement -- of that report. I draw your attention, Professor Aleksandric, to the middle of that paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- the clothing that was found on -- on body number 9, who was ultimately identified as Pal Krasniqi, was described as -- in part as trousers in a blue track suit with vertical patterns in the shape of stripes with one stripe in the middle. I'd just like to draw your attention to Exhibit P559, having that in mind. And if we can -- you see from that exhibit the middle photograph refers to label R-9, it's a piece of clothing. If we can just zoom in on the top photograph, please. Just very briefly can you indicate what that depicts?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the earlier photograph would have been more appropriate because one would be able to see clearly the stripes on the track-suit bottoms. You can see the longitudinal stripes and the letters "OSE".

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then go back to the middle photograph very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see here in the top part, you see the multi-coloured stripes, and it says "USA."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was taken once the clothing had been washed and dried. You have to understand that we dared not to wash the clothing thoroughly because it had already partly disintegrated and decayed. We tried to wash the clothing to rid it of mud and to preserve it in such a condition as would allow for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do want to indicate that I'm about to move into another area which can be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask: Is the identity of R-9, is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No, it's not. It's part of the agreed facts that the DNA analysis, certainly for the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj, is that of Pal Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The purpose of that -- those questions, Your Honour, is that the Chamber may recall that Witness 6 provided a description of the -- of the clothing when Pal Krasniqi was last seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And therefore, it's relevant for the purposes of when he was last seen after he disappeared entirely, not for any identification per se.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say that the clothing in which he was last seen is the clothing he had on his body when his body was retrieved?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that clarification. Then perhaps you could help me out as far as body number R-5 is concerned. What was the issue there? The two autopsy reports to -- well, at least the one autopsy report where it says could have been shot in the head but could have been the shot in the other body as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, as you may have gathered from my friend's objections, there are a series of paragraphs which -- in the 92 ter statement which we've agreed to lead orally with the Defence precisely because they are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we have not been informed about that yet. So that's -- or did we?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was -- I interject here. That was the letter I forwarded to the -- or the e-mail I forwarded to the Trial Chamber and the Defence yesterday where we set --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Morning sometime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: After we met with the Defence and wrote and read in the e-mail those parts we would lead orally after objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then I apologise for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was just indicating that it's almost 10.30 and I was about to go into a bit of a longer area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need a longer area, then perhaps we'll first have a break. We'll have a break. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I was noting that there had been some invitation to deal with the French report and I don't know whether or not that's going to occur or not in terms of the issues to focus upon. There it was something you had raised earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I suggested, Ms. Issa --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps it's something I can address, Your Honour, after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then we'll hear from you after the break. We'll have a break until five minutes 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps before we break, since Mr. Guy-Smith just rose in relation to that suggestion, perhaps he can indicate which bodies concern him in particular with respect to the -- to the French report or -- and if the Trial Chamber has any specific --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I expressed already that not only for one body that conclusions are drawn from the -- let me say then rather vague words, on the presence of certain matters on the bodies and the development of vegetation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are two issues that appear again and again and which seem not have been dealt with by -- by this witness. Let me now just check.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's not limited to one body, but that appears for several bodies. We'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, first of all, before -- I missed, as a matter of fact, the yesterday e-mail. I've got it in front of me now with all the paragraphs. I think I did not pay sufficient attention to it because it was introduced to us by our staff as points of agreement, eight points still remaining as not agreed upon. I also noted that the issue of the bullet-holes on R-5 was -- the objection was withdrawn. So therefore, that seemed not to have been an issue anymore. I have got the list in front of me, Ms. Issa. So whenever we are talking about any of the paragraphs listed here please draw my attention to it and I will try to be more friendly to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the witness proceeds, there's just one matter -- a proposal I would like to make to the Trial Chamber, and that's in relation to how we deal with Professor Lecomte's report and how this witness deals with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The difficulty we have at the moment is, although the report is dated the 15th of June the translation into English is not complete. We hope to have it done -- we're told-- either today, tomorrow, or early next week. The proposal I would make -- I hope that it would address the Trial Chamber's concerns -- would be to go as far as we can today with the witness, maybe another half an hour, provide the English version, the witness speaks pretty good English, the English copy as soon as we get it, give it to the witness, the professor won't be available until August. And then when he comes back, we briefly resume for whatever time it takes, maybe up to half an hour, to put the matters that are of concern which are the most relevant matters in dispute to the witness and finish the re-examination -- sorry, the examination-in-chief then and he moves straight into cross-examination with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I ask the Defence to respond to this, wouldn't it then be better to ask this expert witness to comment in writing because if that is led in additional examination-in-chief, then I know almost for sure that the Defence will say: We need to consult our experts on it and we can't immediately cross-examine. Usually on expert reports there's some time available. Would that be an option -- well, let's say, one week prior to the beginning of cross-examination, would that be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I could say in the remaining time if any of the findings of this expert as they stand in his report at the moment could nevertheless be explored, that may be relevant to the issues that the time could be usefully used in that regard in addition to a further reported being prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, therefore the amended suggestion now is that as soon as the English version is available it will be presented to Professor Aleksandric and that he has an opportunity to comment in writing that would be kind of an additional expert report to be presented to the Defence not later than one week before the start of the cross-examination. Yes. Then I take it that on the basis of all of this that at least one of the parties will tender the new report, the French report, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We will tender that, if it's in e-court, we'll certainly tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, fine. No, that's just that it's clear, because otherwise the Chamber might call that evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just in relation to that -- we would ask that there be some time available, if necessary, for us to examine the professor on his additional report when he returns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If -- if his comments are there in writing, I think that clarification of some of these issues could be done orally as well. That's -- seems to be fair. Yes, it's so decided. Then, Ms. Issa, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, may I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not going to be in my country, in Belgrade, until August the 13th. I will be away, so I would be able to reply in writing only after that date and I kindly ask to be given an adequate amount of time to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that that should not cause major problems, in view of the schedule of the Chamber. So that's -- that's understood. Also, I take it that where usually there should be no communication between the party calling the witness and the witness, once he has given a solemn declaration, that under the circumstances the Prosecution could send an English version of the -- that's then understand. We'll deal with it at the very end. Ms. Issa, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Professor Aleksandric, I want to ask you questions about body R-20 --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the reference of the Chamber, I believe that that's referred to in paragraph 166 in the statement and we've indicated that we would develop the material in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can we just -- if we can just -- actually, before we go there I've forgotten. There's one more thing I wanted to just wrap up from the previous portion of your examination-in-chief, which is, if we could briefly return to Exhibit P506, just to clarify something. That is the photo which should be on your screen, Professor Aleksandric. That was the photo that was the autopsy photo of body 12 with the barbed wire. Can you describe the intermingling of the barbed wire with the body and indicate why the barbed wire was placed on the body in that manner?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that the bulk of the bodies were turned over into the bags, and then as you saw in the photographs shown previously we searched by hand to see if any of the bones remained behind and then searching over the fragments of the bones or the bones, we found the barbed wire. So first we placed the body in the body-bag, and then we didn't bother again to lift the body to place the wire underneath. We would just place the wire or whatever we found on top of the body that was already in the bag, and that -- that is why the order of the things in the bag is like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But just for the record, the barbed wire appears to be around the huge part of the -- of the bones sticking out and it appears to be intermingled with the body as it was placed in the bag. And you're saying that that was the reason was because that was how you placed it in the bag. Just then turning to body R-20 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. From what I can see, it was just put there. Maybe it looks like that in the picture, but it was actually just placed on the body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whatever is the case it was put there at a later stage --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and it doesn't reflect the position in which the barbed wire was when the body was found.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can focus on R-20, please, and who was ultimately identified as Ilija Antic. Professor, I just wanted to refer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps just for the record it now reads -- but perhaps I have been -- perhaps I had a bad pronunciation. It now says: "It doesn't reflect the position of the body when it was found," it is: "On the body -- the barbed wire on the body when the body was found." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Professor, you refer in paragraph 168 to the process of saponification and you define saponification as a particular process of putrification which occurs in moist areas, and you say that it is a process of decomposition where the soft tissue of a body converts into soap. So just focusing on R-20, you indicate in paragraph 164 that this body was found "500 metres downstream, behind a small lake, on the dry part of the canyon, 1 metre above the water surface ... and the body was covered by mud, and in part by large pieces of clay rock." I'd like to show you a clip from P452, a short clip, and I'd like you just to watch that for a second. It starts at 014437.4, and afterwards I will ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we could stop there for a moment, please that's at 014522.5.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate, Professor, what -- can you just describe the previous image that we just saw as to the location in relation to the canyon of body 20?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The body was stuck underneath a rock but it's not a stone rock, it's a clay rock, that kind of soil. So it's placed in the direction of the flow of the water. That's how it lay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. If we can --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very stuck together and pressed by the clay rock from what I can remember, and we were unable to pull it out, get it unstuck from the rock. So we had to cut the rock that was overhanging the body in order to be able to get the body off from the soil. And if I can recall, the body lay stuck in the direction of the stream, of the water, the current.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then just continue with the video-clip, and I'll ask you a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is that the body we're looking at now, at 04530?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that the part of the rock is overhanging the body, and that is why we had to cut away a part of the rock in order to be able to get to the body and pull it away.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the record that's at 014546.1. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, is that -- just if we can stop there briefly, please. Just -- shortly, just a bit before 014617 -- yeah, 0146137, is that the lake -- the small lake that you describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is about 500 metres downstream from the beginning of the natural part of the canyon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then go to the next clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is - stop for a moment, please - at 015048.7, Exhibit 452, for the record. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see how we cut the clay rock that was overhanging the body in order to be able to get to the body, and now you will see how we are trying to get the body unstuck from the surface that it was lying on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's at 05128 [sic].

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if we can stop there for a moment, please, at 015158.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What is that bluish/greenish colour that we see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The surface under the body became that colour in the process of putrefaction and saponification which is a different stage of putrification so the putrefaction liquids were seeping into the bottom surface of the body so that the colour of the clothing also seeped into the clay and it coloured the surface soil which was a clay type of soil. This seepage of the body would indicate that the body had been there for a long time, that it had been in this place for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why is it that this seepage of colour indicates it had been there for a long time?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the colour seeps into the soil for a long time, it soaks into the surface for a long time, the soil becomes discoloured. If it had been there for just a short amount of time, the soil or the surface would not have been discoloured to such an extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can you indicate for how long --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm at this point going to interpose an objection that this is outside of the expertise of the witness. It's dealing -- there are a whole series of factors that exist here. We are now dealing specifically with what we call dyeing of external materials, which is something there is no indication this gentleman has any expertise in, specifically dealing with the issue of clothing and the colour of clothing having been the causative factor for the colour of the soil.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, perhaps if we could have any additional information as to -- for example, the colour of the clothing, whether perhaps you could explore with the expert whether there are any other explanations he could think of, that's not to say that if he can't think of them that they do not exist, but still to be explored. Could you please explore this matter. Mr. Guy-Smith, I do not agree that it's -- it's partly within -- partly perhaps outside of the field of expertise, that is, specific how colour sticks to underground might not be the core of the expertise of this witness; nevertheless, the colour of certain body liquids leaking out of it might well be. So therefore, we are at a juncture of two fields of expertise, where I -- I would allow the witness to -- to explain why he came to certain conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. To the extent it goes outside of his expertise, my concern remains the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It might actually assist Your Honour if we play the video a little longer and then I'll ask the witness a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You can stop there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can explain this now --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that the surface of the soil is coloured exactly within the boundaries that were covered by the body. Can there be any other logical conclusion other than that the colour came from the putrefaction matter and from the clothing of the body?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record that's at 015250.7. And perhaps we can play just slightly longer till the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And as you -- as the body was being placed in the body-bag where we see that there at 05307 [sic]. Did it become disarticulated in any way?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see for yourself when we were lifting the body that what was contained inside the clothing we could transfer into the body-bag in one piece, but in places where the clothing was decayed and very delicate, that place we were not able to pick up with the rest of the body. So it stayed behind so then we were able to turn it over into the body-bag later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And again just for the record the last image we are seeing is a label being placed inside the body-bag at 015326.0. Professor Aleksandric, are you able to give an estimate as to how long this particular body was stuck underneath the rocks, given your findings and observations?

utterances.speaker: BRANIMIR ALEKSANDRIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The body had been there for several weeks, definitely. Don't forget that this was a partly humid and partly dry climate. When there would be water or the current was bigger because of the rain, the body would be wet. And then when -- and that was when the process of decomposition went much faster than it would be if the body was in a dry place. The temperatures also were high. It was the end of the summer, so all of these factors indicate to me that the body had been there for several weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, I'm -- still have some -- a few questions here. Do I understand you well that the colour of the clothing enters into the body and that then the body loses that, perhaps, then mixed liquid and passes it to the soil? Is that how I have to understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
