utterances.text: We are aware of that. Then finally whatever course we'll take, Professor Dunjic, I would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony, the testimony given and still to be given. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, good afternoon. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I had the case called again because it was uncertain when we would resume. Professor Dunjic, fortunately - and I say this with some gratitude - we found all the staff we need to have this court session. So we can conclude your examination-in-chief today. I usually remind witnesses that they are still bound by the solemn declaration, but since you testified this morning I think it goes without saying. I see you are nodding yes. Mr. Dutertre, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Having examined the various objects, Professor, that were found near the victims and the non-deadly injuries, I'd like to discuss now the deadly injuries, in particular the case of body R-9, which is dealt with under Counts 31 and 32. If there are no objections on the part of the Defence, I can give the name of the victim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... That's not relevant. R-9 sufficiently identifies the body we are talking about. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In paragraph 291 of your statement, you indicate the following, and this will be coming up on the screen under Sanction and I'm going to read it out as well: [In English] "There was an entry injury and an exit injury to the head." [Interpretation] I would like to call exhibit under 64 [as interpreted] ter number 867, 867, page 48. This is annex 49 of the consolidated statement. Once the photograph comes up on the screen, Professor, I would like to ask you to tell us whether the photographs you see are, indeed, in relationship to body R-9. It's annex 49. It seems there's a technical problem here. I don't know whether the Defence has a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have a copy of this document, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the interpreters, it's three photographs, in fact.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: The quality of these -- of the document is not excellent, but you do have it in front of you now. Can you confirm that these three photographs relate to a body R-9?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you look at the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have the picture now on our screen. What page is it in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see any image -- it's page 48 of 867 under Rule 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There really seems to be a technical problem to get it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So you have confirmed that these pictures do relate to body R-9. Now, I'd like to ask you to look at the picture in the middle, in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a zoom on this one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And, Professor, I'd like to ask you to comment on this picture. What does the arrow represent?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: This is a picture of the base of the skull, and could I please look at the top photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we take a look at the top photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a shot of the right half of the skull, and this is an injury characteristic of a projectile exit wound. And the one at the base of the skull we noted down as the entry wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When you say "entry" and "exit wound," you're referring to a projectile?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's an injury caused by a projectile from a side-arm or a hand weapon, and the injuries which were caused while the person was still alive probably led to the person's death.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Professor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have Exhibit 65 ter 913, I repeat, 913, page 17.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone. Microphone, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: This is an autopsy report dated 2003 by Dr. Gasior by UNMIK -- from UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we enlarge the part that refers to the summary and the cause of death, please. I would like to note that it has not been contested that this autopsy report relates to body R-9.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, Professor, to read this document. I'm also going to read it out so that you have it in your language translated, and the text states under "cause of death: [In English] "It is my determination that the cause of death in the case number R-RE08/001B was multiple gun-shot injury (to the head, trunk, and upper limbs)." [Interpretation] Professor, my question is as follows: Are these conclusions in agreement with your own conclusions having examined this body?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Since I don't see that this report has any direct link with R-9 but since the multiple gun-shot injury is indicated as the cause of death, I can confirm, since I have before me the findings that we arrived at which was the gun-shot wound to the head, as you were able to see and to the trunk and limbs. Based on that, this conclusion would be consistent with our own findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor. Well, indeed, just for information, for the information of the Chamber, although the reference here is R-RE08/001B there is no disagreement amongst the parties that this autopsy report carried out in 2003 does, indeed, correspond to the body R-9. Generally speaking, Professor, could you tell us how many bullet wounds have you discovered in the autopsies that you carried out between the 12th and 19th of September, 1998, or rather, on how many victims did you find bullet wounds -- gun-shot wounds, rather?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number out of the 39 victims because some of them had two gun-shot or fire-arm wounds. Most of the victims had also gun-shot injuries. On the remains of the bones we were able to examine, there were clearly visible injuries caused by fire-arms and those which were not caused by fire-arm projectiles. This was clearly indicated in all the records, but I cannot give you the exact figure and tell you how many of the 39 victims had gun-shot wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to go on to another issue which is the identification of victims. I'd like to refer to paragraphs 110 and 113, where you explain the identification procedure. In paragraph 113, which we could perhaps have on the screen with Sanction, you state that the clothing had been washed and dried and laid out on tables. Could you tell us why the clothing was washed, the clothing that was discovered with the bodies, why was it washed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: In order to clearly identify such parameters as were able to be found on the clothing, such as colour, pattern, possible damage to the clothing and which would help in identification. Most of the clothing was affected by mud and by the decay to which it was exposed. In order to bring up the colour and pattern of the clothing, we washed every piece of clothing, dried it, and laid it out in order to facilitate the process of identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I've just been told that we can't switch to Sanction right now, which is why the paragraph has not been put up on the screen. I'd like to call up 64 [as interpreted] ter 867, I repeat, 867, page 10. Professor --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And first of all, could we perhaps have a zoom on the upper right-hand picture, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Professor, could you tell us what you can see on the small label that's attached to the piece of clothing on the right-hand side of this screen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: This is a female dress with buttons. It is marked with the same number, R-1, as the body we autopsied. Most of the clothing was washed. At the top and at the bottom there's the darker colour, and this was the discolouring of the clothing caused by the putrification liquid, therefore, caused by the changes in the stages of putrification. But as I said, this is a piece of a female dress.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor, for those details regarding these pieces of clothing. My question relates now to traceability. How could you provide for the traceability of these pieces of clothing while they were being washed? How did you proceed to provide for traceability once the piece of clothing was removed from the bag and you had it washed, how could you be absolutely certain that the right piece of clothing had the appropriate label?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: From the very outset the procedure was such that every stage of the process was photographed. First the body was photographed in the body-bag. As soon as the body was taken out of the body-bag it was photographed again with the same label. Then the clothing and personal effects, if any, were photographed with the same label. Once they were washed and dried - and you have to know that in the area where we left the clothing - we would also leave the corresponding labels so that once the clothes are washed and dried up, they are also labelled and laid out for the relatives to look at in the process of identification. Thus, there was a continuity from the labelling of the body in the body-bag, taking out the body out of the body-bag, washing up and drying up the clothes and their subsequent preservation for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Court's information the reference of R-1 is the body for which request of amendment of the indictment has been requested. Now, Vukosava Markovic was identified by traditional means by the family. This is in paragraph 304 to 309 of the consolidated statement. I would like to see video V0006012. I don't know if it's going to work. For technical reasons, I'm not sure I'm going to be able to show this footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what to say, Mr. Dutertre. If you manage to do it, we'll look at it; if you don't manage to do it -- or is it a problem with the registry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it's a technical problem at the side of the registry, so therefore then let's proceed with what we can show.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So I'll go to another topic, and that will be my last point. My last point is what the fate of these bodies was, after the autopsies what was done with them. Bodies from Dasinovac, their remains were identified by your team, Professor, as being Milos Radunovic and Slobodan Radosevic. This is in paragraph 705 of your statement. Paragraph 709 you indicate this and I shall read it in English: [In English] "At the insistence of the families, bone fragments were laid in caskets with the clothes identified as those as Milos Radunovic and Slobodan Radosevic to avoid burying clothes alone without any remains. All the bones were separated equally into the caskets that were provided by us, that is to say, the remains from at least three individuals." [Interpretation] Professor, on this specific point, that is putting the remains of Dasinovac, showing them to the families, giving them back to the families, could you develop a bit and give more details on the way these remains was -- were given to the families. Could you elaborate? And more specifically, were you in a position to determine which bones belonged to which body or where you in a situation- that's what I think I understood, I'd like to clarify- where you just had to make a choice between the bones?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, we did not make the choice ourselves. The bones were brought together with the clothing, the clothing, therefore, of three males and one female. We received the bones that were recovered in the area of Dasinovac village. We marked them with letter "D". One person had with it the ID documentation to the name of Milos Radunovic, the other to the name of Slobodan Radosevic. And as for the third person, we found trousers that weren't identified by anyone. The fourth person was a woman. We were told that over a very small area the remains of the bones and clothing were found. The -- at the insistence of the sons and relatives, all the clothing and bones that belonged to Milos Radunovic and Slobodan Radosevic were placed in the casket. And the clothing that was together with some small fragments of bone which we were unable to identify to establish the height or anything else, it was agreed with the relatives that these bones as well as this third pair of trousers nobody knew who belonged to would be put together with the remains of these two persons in the casket.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what was the fate of this casket? Could you let us know if you know what became of this casket with small parts -- small bones which you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: I have to indicate that all the bodies, both the identified and unidentified one, we saw them being placed into individual caskets. We were present as this was being done. For those who were not identified, the casket was closed and marked with the same label that we used to mark the body, the clothing, and everything else, the same number. That's to say, the remains were put into a bag and the bag was placed in a casket. The remains of all these unidentified persons were transferred two or three days after we finished our job to a place outside the Orthodox cemetery in Djakovica and were buried there. The required number of graves was dug out, and each of the caskets was placed in the individual grave-sites, which were then labelled. Initially, it was thought that a cross would be placed on the graves; however, since we were unable to establish the ethnicity of the victims the cross was removed and what remained were only vertical pillars labelled "R" and then the corresponding number of that particular body. The same labels were also placed on the caskets themselves, and all of that was photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Professor. Professor, if I do understand what you say - and I stand corrected if I'm not right - the remains which were handed to you as coming from Dasinovac, part of them were given to the families, that the family of Milos Radunovic, the other one to Slobodan Radosevic, and the third part was put with the unidentified bodies. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. All the three bodies were placed in a casket because we weren't able to distinguish between the different parts of the bones. We weren't able to establish what belonged to Radunovic, save for the clothing. We couldn't establish which of the remains of the bones belonged to his body. It was all put together. All the bones were put together in a casket.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what was then given to the families along with the clothing, did that include bones or not to the families of Slobodan Radosevic and Milos Radunovic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: The contents were bones and clothing. I repeat, we could not establish which of the bones belonged to Radunovic and which to Radosevic. We, therefore, only divided the bones equally -- we separated them equally into the caskets, together with the clothing, and we marked them as D-1, D-2, and D-3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you know what became of the non-identified caskets, or rather, the caskets containing the non-identified remains? Were you there when those caskets were taken away and buried or were you told what happened by someone else?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN DUNJIC
utterances.text: This is what I was told. The second time I arrived again for the five bodies that were subsequently uncovered, I was taken to the place where these unidentified bodies were buried and there a photograph of that. There is the photograph of the place where they were buried and there's a photograph showing the way in which this was done. I, myself, wasn't present at the burial of these remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Professor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my last question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This concludes your examination-in-chief, Professor Dunjic. I'd like to give you the same instruction as I did this morning, since cross-examination is still to be awaited. I have a question to the parties in relation to the 23rd of April -- in relation to the French report of the 15th of June. Is there any wish to have the comments of Professor Dunjic as well? Because I noticed that as far as the cause of death is concerned that there seems to be less controversy than in relation to the time and the time is -- especially the time the bodies were there. Nevertheless, Professor Dunjic is now here. So if there would be any wish I could consider to ask Professor Dunjic. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we have about ten seconds to confer?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: That's what I was also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you for the opportunity. There's no particular request on the part of the Defence for that report to be given to Professor Dunjic or any comments from him to be requested at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, I take it you have thoroughly studied the French report. Is there any wish from the side of the Prosecution to have Professor Dunjic comment on the findings in that report?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I will trust fully the Court to -- in that respect. No particular request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Professor Dunjic, you'll receive information on when we would like you to appear again in order to be cross-examined. For the time being I would like to thank you for having come to The Hague and for having answered the questions put to you until now. I wish you a safe trip home again, and looking at the clock it seems to me that you'll make it to be in time at the airport.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I'm grateful to you for your patience in hearing me out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to thank you for waiting and coming back this afternoon. It's highly appreciated that you made yourself available also this afternoon. Thank you very much. Then, since we have a couple of minutes left -- yes, Professor Dunjic, Madam Usher will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to read a rather short decision. I do understand that the booths have been provided with the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a request for the parties concerning witnesses -- two witnesses for which the Trial Chamber issued subpoenas on the 6th and the 7th of June, 2007, subpoenas ad testificandum. On the 21st of June, 2007, memoranda of service were filed in which the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Montenegro confirmed that the witnesses had received the subpoena and while prepared to testify videolink -- via videolink from Montenegro, they were unable or unwilling to travel to The Hague. The applications for subpoena of 1 and 6th of June provide information about the family situation of these witnesses. While it is generally preferable that testimony should be given in court, the Chamber is nevertheless mindful of the need to -- not to place an undue burden on the needs of family members of a witness and believes that in these cases there may be good reasons why the witnesses may be unable or unwilling to travel to The Hague. The Chamber would, therefore, invite the parties to make submissions on whether these two witnesses, of which I do not know whether there will ever be any application for protective measures, should be heard by videolink from Montenegro; and if so, on what -- on which date. The parties are invited to make the submissions orally or in writing - orally might be difficult - within 48 hours. This concludes the request of the Chamber to the parties. Finally, I'd like to inquire into whether the lists of exhibits tendered through the last witnesses, Mr. Dixon, Mr. Guy-Smith, and Mr. Harvey -- oh, Mr. Troop, whether they have been provided to the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they have and I believe they are complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that these exhibits, there were no objections to them when presented to the witness. I urge the parties that since final decisions are made once the witnesses have left The Hague, that if there would be any objection they should be raised at the moment when the exhibits are presented to the witnesses. Because if there are any objections at a later stage, then of course we are unable to ask further questions about it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As far as the exhibits shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's just a reminder on the procedure rather than -- rather than pointing at any specific problem. Mr. Re, Mr. Dutertre, Ms. Issa not being there, no. I overlooked her last time and I'll not make the same mistake again. Is there -- have similar lists been prepared for inspection by the Defence and for adopting this material in the e-court system?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, we have a list of the exhibits for both witnesses. I think the Defence has it. Mr. Guy-Smith's nodding. We'll certainly provide it to the registry if we haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that we can deal with them as soon as we are sitting again. That means, if there are no other procedural matters to be raised, they should be raised now because it's until the 16th that we are not sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: There is one brief matter and that is in respect of the last witness, Professor Aleksandric, there is some tidying to do on his Rule 92 ter statement. Your Honour will recall there were some objections and the Prosecution conceded some of those but there were others that were left and there was testimony given in chief and objections heard. And based on the guidance given by the Trial Chamber, the proposal would be to attempt between the parties to tidy up that statement and then to have it presented. It has been marked for identification but then presented to be formally tendered once that has been done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The final one --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: If there are any outstanding issues, those can then be raised, hopefully, it can be done through agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you know disagreement about 92 ter statements are dealt with at 10.00 at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to encourage you to resolve the matter during the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's one matter I would like to briefly raise and that's the following. Mr. Re, the expert report by Mr. Visnjic, that was annex 63, I think, to the -- to the last witness of fact, Mr. Avramovic. We did not admit that. Is there any application to -- or are you preparing any application to call Mr. Visnjic as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We have filed an application for his report to be accepted under Rule 94 bis as an expert. The implication of that would be if the Defence wish to cross-examine him, he would be called to testify we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to remind me, when was this filed? Is this the early series in 12th of January --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It was last week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last week. Okay. Yes. So you do not intend to call him as a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, yes and no. In the sense that he would be a witness for the Prosecution, yes; but in the sense of him actually coming to court and testifying, only if the Defence requested to -- requested that he be cross-examined. If that's the case, they've got the 30 days. I assume they do. If they do want him to be cross-examined, we would apply to have him as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, I do understand that further submissions will be made by the -- by the Defence on this matter. If, of course, now we have to wait for the 30 days whether or not to accept the report, qualifications, et cetera, if you -- I take it that you have to file anyhow an application to have your witness list amended because from what I understand you had forgotten one witness on your most recent version. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A witness disappeared in the proofreading, yes, and put back on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would strongly suggest that in addition to a request to have the Visnjic report admitted under Rule 94 bis, also perhaps as an alternative, to apply for an amendment of your witness list so that Mr. Visnjic would appear as a witness. And then of course the Defence could respond to that motion, to that request, and then include whatever it would like to say in respect, both of Mr. Visnjic as an expert, to comment on his report -- well, whatever is relevant in relation to Mr. Visnjic and the report that was originally attached as annex 63 to the 92 ter statement of Mr. Avramovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll file that by Monday. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Monday's fine. Yes. Then if there's no other matter, we'll adjourn until the 16th of July, 9.00 in the morning, this same courtroom.
